**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (a `feat`: merges at the next cut). No blockers found.

**What looks good**
- One door, no second write path: `edit_machine` builds `LoadMachine::new` (document) or `SetSetupMachine::new` (a setup's own machine), the same commands the Machine window's Apply pushes. Both refuse `!Machine::is_sane()` at creation (`commands/load_machine.rs:30`, `setup_mount.rs:64`), so travel limits, spindle range, axes, rotary and the EDM bounds all apply to a patched machine before it is mounted. `crates/app/src/mcp/machine_tools.rs:90-101`. One undo restores the whole machine (tested undo/redo).
- Merge-patch semantics are stated in the tool description and the decision note (RFC 7396: object merges, null removes, other value replaces) and tested (null removes `pickup`).
- Unknown keys are refused by name, not stored: the merged value is deserialized, re-serialized, and any patch key that did not survive is reported (`unknown key 'edm.orbit_radius'`, `'bogus'`). Tested at top level and inside `edm`. A kind/key mismatch (wire key on a sinker) is refused via `Edm::fits`.
- A refused patch changes nothing and a no-op patch is refused (test compares `get_job` machine before/after). Errors are `Result<_, String>`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in product code.
- The post-crate change is purely additive: new `Edm::refusal()` in `edm_named.rs` (provenance line present), one `mod` line, no existing function touched. It mirrors `Edm::is_sane` check by check and names the key.
- Tool is in the server table (`tools.rs:71`) and `tools/list` is asserted; `get_job` gains `machine {path, definition}` for read-back. Files are small; decision note present; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1162`; no CHANGELOG/process/snapshot files touched.

**Local results** (PR head trial-merged with current origin/main, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| app `mcp_edit_machine` | 3 passed |
| app `machine_edit` | 12 passed |
| app `machine` | 33 passed |
| app `edm_machine` | 5 passed |
| app `edm_conditions` | 1 passed |
| app `mcp` | 18 passed |
| app `machine_switch` (post re-judge on machine change) | 6 passed |
| post `--lib` | 38 passed |
| post `mch_head_search`, `vendor_mch_cli` | 2 + 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The camcraft-mcp skill row (a process file, `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`) is not added; the PR body says "maintainer follow-up" but names no issue. Either add the row with a `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` bump (main is at 31 -> 32) or file and name a `source:agent` follow-up issue (`P5`, `area:mcp`) so it is not lost.
2. `Edm::refusal()` duplicates `Edm::is_sane` rule by rule; the two can drift. A small unit test asserting `refusal().is_none() == is_sane()` over a few bad sections (or having `is_sane` call `refusal`) would pin it. Not a safety gap today: `is_sane` still gates at the command.
3. Non-EDM refusals (travel, spindle range, rotary) come from the command's own `is_sane` check, so they are refused and leave the machine unchanged, but are not named by key like the `edm.*` ones, and no test covers them. A non-EDM case in `mcp_edit_machine.rs` would show it.
4. No test covers the post being re-judged after an `edit_machine` that tightens a limit. Structurally it is the same mount path `machine_switch.rs` pins, so it should hold, but an edit-flavoured case would make that explicit.
5. The issue also names `edm.codes`; the decision note explains the tree has no such field. Fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
